11: 
12: By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
13: 
14: This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
15: 
16: > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).
17: 
18: ## When to use Server and Client Components?
19: 
20: The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.
21: 
22: Use **Client Components** when you need:
23: 
24: - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.
25: - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.
26: - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.
27: - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).
28: 
29: Use **Server Components** when you need:
30: 
31: - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.
32: - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.
33: - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
34: - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.
35: 
36: For example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.
37: 
38: ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,17} switcher
39: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
40: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
41: 
42: export default async function Page({
43:   params,
44: }: {
45:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
46: }) {
47:   const { id } = await params
48:   const post = await getPost(id)
49: 
50:   return (
51:     <div>
52:       <main>
53:         <h1>{post.title}</h1>
54:         {/* ... */}
55:         <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
56:       </main>
57:     </div>
58:   )
59: }
60: ```
61: 
62: ```jsx filename="app/[id]/page.js" highlight={1,13} switcher
63: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
64: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
65: 
66: export default async function Page({ params }) {
67:   const { id } = await params
68:   const post = await getPost(id)
69: 
70:   return (
71:     <div>
72:       <main>
73:         <h1>{post.title}</h1>
74:         {/* ... */}
75:         <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
76:       </main>
77:     </div>
78:   )
79: }
80: ```
81: 
82: ```tsx filename="app/ui/like-button.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
83: 'use client'
84: 
85: import { useState } from 'react'
86: 
87: export default function LikeButton({ likes }: { likes: number }) {
88:   // ...
89: }
90: ```
91: 
92: ```jsx filename="app/ui/like-button.js" highlight={1} switcher
93: 'use client'
94: 
95: import { useState } from 'react'
96: 
97: export default function LikeButton({ likes }) {
98:   // ...
99: }
100: ```
101: 
102: ## How do Server and Client Components work in Next.js?
103: 
104: ### On the server
105: 
106: On the server, Next.js uses React's APIs to orchestrate rendering. The rendering work is split into chunks, by individual route segments ([layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages)), including [parallel route slots](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) whether or not they are displayed:
107: 
108: - **Server Components** are rendered into a special data format called the React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload).
109: - **Client Components** and the RSC Payload are used to [prerender](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) HTML.
110: 
111: > **What is the React Server Component Payload (RSC)?**
112: >
113: > The RSC Payload is a compact, serialized representation of the rendered React Server Components tree. It's used by React on the client to update the browser's DOM. The RSC Payload contains:
114: >
115: > - The rendered result of Server Components
116: > - Placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files
117: > - Any props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component
118: 
119: ### On the client (first load)
120: 
121: Then, on the client:
122: 
123: 1. **HTML** is used to immediately show a fast non-interactive preview of the route to the user.
124: 2. **RSC Payload** is used to reconcile the Client and Server Component trees.
125: 3. **JavaScript** is used to hydrate Client Components and make the application interactive.
126: 
127: > **What is hydration?**
128: >
129: > Hydration is React's process for attaching [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events) to the DOM, to make the static HTML interactive.
130: 
131: ### Subsequent Navigations
132: 
133: On subsequent navigations:
134: 
135: - The **RSC Payload** is prefetched and cached for instant navigation.
136: - **Client Components** are rendered entirely on the client, without the server-rendered HTML.
137: 
138: ## Examples
139: 
140: ### Using Client Components
141: 
142: You can create a Client Component by adding the [`"use client"`](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) directive at the top of the file, above your imports.
143: 
144: ```tsx filename="app/ui/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
145: 'use client'
146: 
147: import { useState } from 'react'
148: 
149: export default function Counter() {
150:   const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
151: 
152:   return (
153:     <div>
154:       <p>{count} likes</p>
155:       <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Click me</button>
156:     </div>
157:   )
158: }
159: ```
160: 
161: ```jsx filename="app/ui/counter.js" highlight={1} switcher
162: 'use client'
163: 
164: import { useState } from 'react'
165: 
166: export default function Counter() {
167:   const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
168: 
169:   return (
170:     <div>
171:       <p>{count} likes</p>
172:       <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Click me</button>
173:     </div>
174:   )
175: }
176: ```
177: 
178: `"use client"` is used to declare a **boundary** between the Server and Client module graphs (trees).
179: 
180: Once a file is marked with `"use client"`, **all of its imports and the components it directly renders are included in the client bundle**. This means you don’t need to add the directive to every component that is intended for the client.
181: 
182: This behavior applies to components that are part of the Client Component’s [module graph](/docs/app/glossary#module-graph), which includes the modules it imports and the components it renders directly. It does not apply to Server Components passed as children or other props. Those components are not imported into the Client Component’s module graph. They are rendered on the server and passed to the Client Component as rendered output.
183: 
184: See [Interleaving Server and Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#interleaving-server-and-client-components) for how Server and Client Components can be combined.
185: 
186: ### Reducing JS bundle size
187: 
188: To reduce the size of your client JavaScript bundles, add `'use client'` at the top of the files that define your interactive components instead of marking large parts of your UI as Client Components.
189: 
190: For example, the `<Layout>` component contains mostly static elements like a logo and navigation links, but includes an interactive search bar. `<Search />` needs to be a Client Component, while the rest of the layout can stay a Server Component.
191: 
192: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={12} switcher
193: // Client Component
194: import Search from './search'
195: // Server Component
196: import Logo from './logo'
197: 
198: // Layout is a Server Component by default
199: export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
200:   return (
201:     <>
202:       <nav>
203:         <Logo />
204:         <Search />
205:       </nav>
206:       <main>{children}</main>
207:     </>
208:   )
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={12} switcher
213: // Client Component
214: import Search from './search'
215: // Server Component
216: import Logo from './logo'
217: 
218: // Layout is a Server Component by default
219: export default function Layout({ children }) {
220:   return (
221:     <>
222:       <nav>
223:         <Logo />
224:         <Search />
225:       </nav>
226:       <main>{children}</main>
227:     </>
228:   )
229: }
230: ```
231: 
232: ```tsx filename="app/ui/search.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
233: 'use client'
234: 
235: export default function Search() {
236:   // ...
237: }
238: ```
239: 
240: ```jsx filename="app/ui/search.js" highlight={1} switcher
241: 'use client'
242: 
243: export default function Search() {
244:   // ...
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: ### Passing data from Server to Client Components
249: 
250: You can pass data from Server Components to Client Components using props.
251: 
252: ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,12} switcher
253: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
254: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
255: 
256: export default async function Page({
257:   params,
258: }: {
259:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
260: }) {
261:   const { id } = await params
262:   const post = await getPost(id)
263: 
264:   return <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
265: }
266: ```
267: 
268: ```jsx filename="app/[id]/page.js" highlight={1,8} switcher
269: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
270: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
271: 
272: export default async function Page({ params }) {
273:   const { id } = await params
274:   const post = await getPost(id)
275: 
276:   return <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
277: }
278: ```
279: 
280: ```tsx filename="app/ui/like-button.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
281: 'use client'
282: 
283: export default function LikeButton({ likes }: { likes: number }) {
284:   // ...
285: }
286: ```
287: 
288: ```jsx filename="app/ui/like-button.js" highlight={1} switcher
289: 'use client'
290: 
291: export default function LikeButton({ likes }) {
292:   // ...
293: }
294: ```
295: 
296: Alternatively, you can stream data from a Server Component to a Client Component with the [`use` API](https://react.dev/reference/react/use). See an [example](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#streaming-data-with-the-use-api).
297: 
298: > **Good to know**: Props passed to Client Components need to be [serializable](https://react.dev/reference/react/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) by React.
299: 
300: ### Interleaving Server and Client Components
301: 
302: You can pass Server Components as a prop to a Client Component. This allows you to visually nest server-rendered UI within Client components.
303: 
304: A common pattern is to use `children` to create a _slot_ in a `<ClientComponent>`. For example, a `<Cart>` component that fetches data on the server, inside a `<Modal>` component that uses client state to toggle visibility.
305: 
306: ```tsx filename="app/ui/modal.tsx" switcher
307: 'use client'
308: 
309: export default function Modal({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
310:   return <div>{children}</div>
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ```jsx filename="app/ui/modal.js" switcher
315: 'use client'
316: 
317: export default function Modal({ children }) {
318:   return <div>{children}</div>
319: }
320: ```
321: 
322: Then, in a parent Server Component (e.g.`<Page>`), you can pass a `<Cart>` as the child of the `<Modal>`:
323: 
324: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"  highlight={7} switcher
325: import Modal from './ui/modal'
326: import Cart from './ui/cart'
327: 
328: export default function Page() {
329:   return (
330:     <Modal>
331:       <Cart />
332:     </Modal>
333:   )
334: }
335: ```
336: 
337: ```jsx filename="app/page.js" highlight={7} switcher
338: import Modal from './ui/modal'
339: import Cart from './ui/cart'
340: 
341: export default function Page() {
342:   return (
343:     <Modal>
344:       <Cart />
345:     </Modal>
346:   )
347: }
348: ```
349: 
350: In this pattern, Server Components are rendered on the server ahead of time, even when passed as props to Client Components. The React Server Component Payload contains the rendered result of those Server Components, plus placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files.
351: 
352: ### Context providers
353: 
354: [React context](https://react.dev/learn/passing-data-deeply-with-context) is commonly used to share global state like the current theme. However, React context is not supported in Server Components.
355: 
356: To use context, create a Client Component that accepts `children`:
357: 
358: ```tsx filename="app/theme-provider.tsx" switcher
359: 'use client'
360: 
361: import { createContext } from 'react'
362: 
363: export const ThemeContext = createContext({})
364: 
365: export default function ThemeProvider({
366:   children,
367: }: {
368:   children: React.ReactNode
369: }) {
370:   return <ThemeContext.Provider value="dark">{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>
371: }
372: ```
373: 
374: ```jsx filename="app/theme-provider.js" switcher
375: 'use client'
376: 
377: import { createContext } from 'react'
378: 
379: export const ThemeContext = createContext({})
380: 
381: export default function ThemeProvider({ children }) {
382:   return <ThemeContext.Provider value="dark">{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>
383: }
384: ```
385: 
386: Then, import it into a Server Component (e.g. `layout`):
387: 
388: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
389: import ThemeProvider from './theme-provider'
390: 
391: export default function RootLayout({
392:   children,
393: }: {
394:   children: React.ReactNode
395: }) {
396:   return (
397:     <html>
398:       <body>
399:         <ThemeProvider>{children}</ThemeProvider>
400:       </body>
401:     </html>
402:   )
403: }
404: ```
405: 
406: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
407: import ThemeProvider from './theme-provider'
408: 
409: export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
410:   return (
411:     <html>
412:       <body>
413:         <ThemeProvider>{children}</ThemeProvider>
414:       </body>
415:     </html>
416:   )
417: }
418: ```
419: 
420: Your Server Component will now be able to directly render your provider, and all other Client Components throughout your app will be able to consume this context.
421: 
422: > **Good to know**: You should render providers as deep as possible in the tree – notice how `ThemeProvider` only wraps `{children}` instead of the entire `<html>` document. This makes it easier for Next.js to optimize the static parts of your Server Components.
423: 
424: To pass server-fetched data through context and read it in Client Components with `use()`, see [Using React's `use` within a Context Provider](/docs/app/guides/single-page-applications#using-reacts-use-within-a-context-provider).
425: 
426: ### Third-party components
427: 
428: When using a third-party component that relies on client-only features, you can wrap it in a Client Component to ensure it works as expected.
429: 
430: For example, the `<Carousel />` can be imported from the `acme-carousel` package. This component uses `useState`, but the module that defines it doesn't yet have the `"use client"` directive.
431: 
432: If you use `<Carousel />` within a Client Component, it will work as expected:
433: 
434: ```tsx filename="app/gallery.tsx" switcher
435: 'use client'
436: 
437: import { useState } from 'react'
438: import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel'
439: 
440: export default function Gallery() {
441:   const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
442: 
443:   return (
444:     <div>
445:       <button onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)}>View pictures</button>
446:       {/* Works, since Carousel is used within a Client Component */}
447:       {isOpen && <Carousel />}
448:     </div>
449:   )
450: }
451: ```
452: 
453: ```jsx filename="app/gallery.js" switcher
454: 'use client'
455: 
456: import { useState } from 'react'
457: import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel'
458: 
459: export default function Gallery() {
460:   const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
461: 
462:   return (
463:     <div>
464:       <button onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)}>View pictures</button>
465:       {/*  Works, since Carousel is used within a Client Component */}
466:       {isOpen && <Carousel />}
467:     </div>
468:   )
469: }
470: ```
471: 
472: However, if you try to use it directly within a Server Component, you'll see an error. This is because Next.js doesn't know `<Carousel />` is using client-only features.
473: 
474: To fix this, you can wrap third-party components that rely on client-only features in your own Client Components:
475: 
476: ```tsx filename="app/carousel.tsx" switcher
477: 'use client'
478: 
479: import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel'
480: 
481: export default Carousel
482: ```
483: 
484: ```jsx filename="app/carousel.js" switcher
485: 'use client'
486: 
487: import { Carousel } from 'acme-carousel'
488: 
489: export default Carousel
490: ```
491: 
492: Now, you can use `<Carousel />` directly within a Server Component:
493: 
494: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
495: import Carousel from './carousel'
496: 
497: export default function Page() {
498:   return (
499:     <div>
500:       <p>View pictures</p>
501:       {/*  Works, since Carousel is a Client Component */}
502:       <Carousel />
503:     </div>
504:   )
505: }
506: ```
507: 
508: ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
509: import Carousel from './carousel'
510: 
511: export default function Page() {
512:   return (
513:     <div>
514:       <p>View pictures</p>
515:       {/*  Works, since Carousel is a Client Component */}
516:       <Carousel />
517:     </div>
518:   )
519: }
520: ```
521: 
522: > **Advice for Library Authors**
523: >
524: > If you’re building a component library, add the `"use client"` directive to entry points that rely on client-only features. This lets your users import components into Server Components without needing to create wrappers.
525: >
526: > It's worth noting some bundlers might strip out `"use client"` directives. You can find an example of how to configure esbuild to include the `"use client"` directive in the [React Wrap Balancer](https://github.com/shuding/react-wrap-balancer/blob/main/tsup.config.ts#L10-L13) and [Vercel Analytics](https://github.com/vercel/analytics/blob/main/packages/web/tsup.config.js#L26-L30) repositories.
527: 
528: ### Preventing environment poisoning
529: 
530: JavaScript modules can be shared between both Server and Client Components modules. This means it's possible to accidentally import server-only code into the client. For example, consider the following function:
531: 
532: ```ts filename="lib/data.ts" switcher
533: export async function getData() {
534:   const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', {
535:     headers: {
536:       authorization: <REDACTED>,
537:     },
538:   })
539: 
540:   return res.json()
541: }
542: ```
543: 
544: ```js filename="lib/data.js" switcher
545: export async function getData() {
546:   const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', {
547:     headers: {
548:       authorization: <REDACTED>,
549:     },
550:   })
551: 
552:   return res.json()
553: }
554: ```
555: 
556: This function contains an `API_KEY` that should never be exposed to the client.
557: 
558: In Next.js, only environment variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are included in the client bundle. If variables are not prefixed, Next.js replaces them with an empty string.
559: 
560: As a result, even though `getData()` can be imported and executed on the client, it won't work as expected.
561: 
562: To prevent accidental usage in Client Components, you can use the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only).
563: 
564: Then, import the package into a file that contains server-only code:
565: 
566: ```js filename="lib/data.js"
567: import 'server-only'
568: 
569: export async function getData() {
570:   const res = await fetch('https://external-service.com/data', {
571:     headers: {
572:       authorization: <REDACTED>,
573:     },
574:   })
575: 
576:   return res.json()
577: }
578: ```
579: 
580: Now, if you try to import the module into a Client Component, there will be a build-time error.
581: 
582: The corresponding [`client-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/client-only) can be used to mark modules that contain client-only logic like code that accesses the `window` object.
583: 
584: In Next.js, installing `server-only` or `client-only` is **optional**. However, if your linting rules flag extraneous dependencies, you may install them to avoid issues.

586: ```bash package="npm"

593: 
594: ```bash package="pnpm"

597: 
598: ```bash package="bun"

600: ```
601: 
602: Next.js handles `server-only` and `client-only` imports internally to provide clearer error messages when a module is used in the wrong environment. The contents of these packages from NPM are not used by Next.js.
603: 
604: Next.js also provides its own type declarations for `server-only` and `client-only`, for TypeScript configurations where [`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#noUncheckedSideEffectImports) is active.

293:               call.ok ? "bg-emerald-500" : "bg-rose-500",
294:             )}
295:           />
296:           <code className="font-mono text-xs text-slate-800">{call.name}</code>
297:         </div>
298:         {call.error ? (
299:           <p className="mt-1 pl-4 text-xs text-rose-600">{call.error}</p>
300:         ) : call.result_summary ? (
301:           <p className="mt-1 pl-4 text-xs text-slate-500">
302:             {call.result_summary}
303:           </p>
304:         ) : null}
305:       </div>
306:       <span className="shrink-0 font-mono text-[11px] text-slate-400">
307:         {formatDuration(call.duration_ms)}
308:       </span>
309:     </div>
310:   );
311: }

313: /** Human labels for the AI-assisted stages. */
314: const AI_STAGE_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
315:   ai_execution_plan: "AI execution planning",
316:   ai_account_mapping: "AI account-mapping investigation",
317:   ai_anomaly_investigation: "AI anomaly investigation",
318:   ai_intercompany_matching: "AI intercompany candidate matching",
319: };
320: 
321: /** Presentation metadata for an AI stage's explicit availability status. */
322: const AI_STAGE_META: Record<
323:   string,
324:   { label: string; badge: string; dot: string }
325: > = {
326:   completed: {
327:     label: "Ran",
328:     badge: "bg-violet-50 text-violet-700 ring-1 ring-violet-600/20",
329:     dot: "bg-violet-500",
330:   },
331:   not_configured: {
332:     label: "AI not configured",
333:     badge: "bg-slate-100 text-slate-600 ring-1 ring-slate-500/20",
334:     dot: "bg-slate-400",
335:   },
336:   failed: {
337:     label: "Failed",
338:     badge: "bg-rose-50 text-rose-700 ring-1 ring-rose-600/20",
339:     dot: "bg-rose-500",
340:   },
341:   skipped: {
342:     label: "Skipped",
343:     badge: "bg-slate-100 text-slate-600 ring-1 ring-slate-500/20",
344:     dot: "bg-slate-300",
345:   },
346: };
347: 
348: function aiStageLabel(stage: string): string {
349:   return AI_STAGE_LABELS[stage] ?? titleCase(stage);
350: }
351: 
352: /** Total latency and token usage across a stage's recorded LLM calls. */
353: function summarizeCalls(stage: AIStage): {
354:   calls: number;
355:   failed: number;
356:   latencyMs: number;
357:   tokens: number | null;
358: } {
359:   const calls = stage.call_records ?? [];
360:   const latencyMs = calls.reduce((sum, c) => sum + (c.latency_ms ?? 0), 0);
361:   const tokens = calls.reduce(
362:     (sum, c) => sum + (c.total_tokens ?? 0),
363:     calls.length > 0 ? 0 : 0,
364:   );
365:   return {
366:     calls: calls.length,
367:     failed: calls.filter((c) => !c.ok).length,
368:     latencyMs,
369:     tokens: tokens > 0 ? tokens : null,
370:   };
371: }
372: 
373: function AIStageRow({ stage }: { stage: AIStage }) {
374:   const meta = AI_STAGE_META[stage.status] ?? AI_STAGE_META.skipped;
375:   const summary = summarizeCalls(stage);
376:   return (
377:     <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-4 py-2.5">
378:       <div className="flex min-w-0 items-start gap-3">
379:         <span className={cn("mt-1.5 size-2 shrink-0 rounded-full", meta.dot)} />
380:         <div className="min-w-0">
381:           <p className="text-sm font-medium text-slate-800">
382:             {aiStageLabel(stage.stage)}
383:           </p>
384:           {stage.detail ? (
385:             <p className="mt-0.5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-slate-500">
386:               {stage.detail}
387:             </p>
388:           ) : null}
389:           {summary.calls > 0 ? (
390:             <p className="mt-0.5 font-mono text-[11px] text-slate-400">
391:               {summary.calls} LLM call{summary.calls === 1 ? "" : "s"}
392:               {summary.failed > 0 ? ` · ${summary.failed} failed` : ""}
393:               {summary.latencyMs > 0
394:                 ? ` · ${formatDuration(summary.latencyMs)}`
395:                 : ""}
396:               {summary.tokens ? ` · ${summary.tokens} tokens` : ""}
397:             </p>
398:           ) : null}
399:         </div>
400:       </div>
401:       <span
402:         className={cn(
403:           "inline-flex shrink-0 rounded-4xl px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium",
404:           meta.badge,
405:         )}
406:       >
407:         {meta.label}
408:       </span>
409:     </div>
410:   );
411: }
412: 
413: function MappingProposalRow({ proposal }: { proposal: AIMappingProposal }) {
414:   return (
415:     <div className="border-b border-slate-100 py-3 last:border-0">
416:       <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
417:         <span className="text-xs font-medium text-slate-700">
418:           Entity {proposal.entity} · account {proposal.local_code}
419:         </span>
420:         {proposal.verified ? null : (
421:           <span className="inline-flex rounded-4xl bg-rose-50 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-rose-700 ring-1 ring-rose-600/20">
422:             Unverified
423:           </span>
424:         )}
425:         <span className="inline-flex rounded-4xl bg-slate-100 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-slate-600">
426:           confidence {proposal.confidence}
427:         </span>
428:         {proposal.needs_human_review ? (
429:           <span className="inline-flex rounded-4xl bg-amber-50 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-amber-700 ring-1 ring-amber-600/20">
430:             Human review required
431:           </span>
432:         ) : null}
433:       </div>
434:       <p className="mt-1.5 text-sm text-slate-700">
435:         Proposed: group account{" "}
436:         <code className="font-mono text-xs text-slate-800">
437:           {proposal.current_group_code ?? "—"}
438:         </code>
439:         {proposal.proposed_group_code ? (
440:           <>
441:             {" → "}
442:             <code className="font-mono text-xs text-slate-800">
443:               {proposal.proposed_group_code}
444:             </code>
445:             {proposal.proposed_group_name
446:               ? ` (${proposal.proposed_group_name})`
447:               : ""}
448:           </>
449:         ) : (
450:           " (no change proposed)"
451:         )}
452:       </p>
453:       {proposal.reasoning ? (
454:         <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-slate-500">{proposal.reasoning}</p>
455:       ) : null}
456:       {proposal.verification_notes ? (
457:         <p className="mt-0.5 text-[11px] text-slate-400">
458:           Verification: {proposal.verification_notes}
459:         </p>
460:       ) : null}
461:       <p className="mt-0.5 text-[11px] text-slate-400">
462:         Advisory only — the deterministic mapping is never changed automatically.
463:       </p>
464:     </div>
465:   );
466: }

468: function MatchProposalRow({ proposal }: { proposal: AIMatchProposal }) {
469:   return (
470:     <div className="border-b border-slate-100 py-3 last:border-0">
471:       <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
472:         <span className="font-mono text-xs text-slate-700">
473:           rows {proposal.left_row} · {proposal.right_row}
474:         </span>
475:         <span
476:           className={cn(
477:             "inline-flex rounded-4xl px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium",
478:             proposal.accepted
479:               ? "bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700 ring-1 ring-emerald-600/20"
480:               : "bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 ring-1 ring-amber-600/20",
481:           )}
482:         >
483:           {proposal.accepted ? "Verified" : "Not accepted"}
484:         </span>
485:         <span className="inline-flex rounded-4xl bg-slate-100 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-slate-600">
486:           {proposal.match_type.replace(/_/g, " ")}
487:         </span>
488:         {proposal.confidence ? (
489:           <span className="text-xs text-slate-500">
490:             confidence {proposal.confidence}
491:           </span>
492:         ) : null}
493:       </div>
494:       {proposal.residual ? (
495:         <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-slate-600">
496:           Residual: {formatAmount(proposal.residual)}
497:           {proposal.reporting_currency
498:             ? ` ${proposal.reporting_currency}`
499:             : ""}
500:         </p>
501:       ) : null}
502:       {proposal.reason ? (
503:         <p className="mt-0.5 text-xs text-slate-500">{proposal.reason}</p>
504:       ) : null}
505:     </div>
506:   );
507: }

509: export function ConsolidationDashboard() {
510:   const [run, setRun] = useState<ConsolidationRun | null>(null);
511:   const [trace, setTrace] = useState<ConsolidationTrace | null>(null);
512:   const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
513:   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
514: 
515:   const loadTrace = useCallback(async (runId: string) => {
516:     try {
517:       setTrace(await getConsolidationTrace(runId));
518:     } catch {
519:       setTrace(null);
520:     }
521:   }, []);
522: 
523:   const runConsolidation = useCallback(async () => {
524:     setRunning(true);
525:     setError(null);
526:     setTrace(null);
527:     try {
528:       const started = await startConsolidationRun();
529:       setRun(started);
530:       await loadTrace(started.run_id);
531:       // Reflect the run id in the URL so a refresh reloads the same run.
532:       const url = new URL(window.location.href);
533:       url.searchParams.set("run", started.run_id);
534:       window.history.replaceState(null, "", url.toString());
535:     } catch (err) {
536:       if (err instanceof ConsolidationApiError) {
537:         setError(err.message);
538:         if (err.body) {
539:           setRun(err.body);
540:           await loadTrace(err.body.run_id);
541:         }
542:       } else {
543:         setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Consolidation failed");
544:       }
545:     } finally {
546:       setRunning(false);
547:     }
548:   }, [loadTrace]);
549: 
550:   // Refresh path: if the URL carries a run id, load the persisted run.
551:   useEffect(() => {
552:     const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
553:     const runId = params.get("run");
554:     if (!runId) return;
555:     let cancelled = false;
556:     (async () => {
557:       try {
558:         const loaded = await getConsolidationRun(runId);
559:         if (cancelled) return;
560:         setRun(loaded);
561:         await loadTrace(runId);
562:       } catch {
563:         if (!cancelled) setError(`Run ${runId} could not be loaded`);
564:       }
565:     })();
566:     return () => {
567:       cancelled = true;
568:     };
569:   }, [loadTrace]);
570: 
571:   const readiness = run?.readiness ?? null;
572:   const entityOrder = ["US", "UK", "IN"];
573:   const entityKeys = readiness
574:     ? [
575:         ...entityOrder.filter((k) => k in readiness.entities_detail),
576:         ...Object.keys(readiness.entities_detail).filter(
577:           (k) => !entityOrder.includes(k),
578:         ),
579:       ]
580:     : [];
581: 
582:   return (
583:     <div className="space-y-6">
584:       {/* A. Header */}
585:       <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between">
586:         <div className="flex items-start gap-3.5">
587:           <span className="mt-0.5 flex size-10 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-[#0a1428] text-blue-400 ring-1 ring-slate-900/10">
588:             <BarChart3 className="size-5" aria-hidden />
589:           </span>
590:           <div>
591:             <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2.5">
592:               <h1 className="text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-slate-900">
593:                 Group Consolidation
594:               </h1>
595:               {run ? <RunStatusBadge status={run.status} /> : null}
596:             </div>
597:             <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500">
598:               Reporting period{" "}
599:               <span className="font-medium text-slate-700">
600:                 {readiness ? `FY${readiness.period}` : "FY2024"}
601:               </span>{" "}
602:               · Presentation currency{" "}
603:               <span className="font-medium text-slate-700">
604:                 {readiness?.functional_currency ?? "GBP"}
605:               </span>
606:             </p>
607:           </div>
608:         </div>
609:         <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
610:           <Button
611:             onClick={runConsolidation}
612:             disabled={running}
613:             aria-busy={running}
614:           >
615:             {running ? (
616:               <Loader2 className="size-4 animate-spin" aria-hidden />
617:             ) : (
618:               <PlayCircle className="size-4" aria-hidden />
619:             )}
620:             {running ? "Running consolidation…" : "Run Consolidation"}
621:           </Button>
622:         </div>
623:       </div>
624: 
625:       {error ? (
626:         <div
627:           role="alert"
628:           className="flex items-start gap-2 rounded-lg border border-rose-200 bg-rose-50 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-rose-700"
629:         >
630:           <AlertTriangle className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
631:           <span>{error}</span>
632:         </div>
633:       ) : null}
634: 
635:       {run ? (
636:         <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-1 text-xs text-slate-500">
637:           <span>
638:             Run ID <code className="font-mono text-slate-700">{run.run_id}</code>
639:           </span>
640:           <span>
641:             Trace{" "}
642:             <code className="font-mono text-slate-700">{run.trace_id}</code>
643:           </span>
644:           <span>
645:             Started{" "}
646:             {run.created_at
647:               ? new Date(run.created_at).toLocaleString("en-GB")
648:               : "—"}
649:           </span>
650:         </div>
651:       ) : null}
652: 
653:       {/* B. Entity overview */}
654:       <Card>
655:         <CardHeader>
656:           <CardTitle>Entities</CardTitle>
657:           <CardDescription>
658:             Group entities with their functional currency and actual
659:             validation / mapping status from the backend run.
660:           </CardDescription>
661:         </CardHeader>
662:         <CardContent>
663:           {readiness && entityKeys.length > 0 ? (
664:             <div className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
665:               {entityKeys.map((key) => (
666:                 <EntityCard
667:                   key={key}
668:                   entity={readiness.entities_detail[key]}
669:                 />
670:               ))}
671:             </div>
672:           ) : (
673:             <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">
674:               Run a consolidation to load entity statuses.
675:             </p>
676:           )}
677:         </CardContent>
678:       </Card>
679: 
680:       {/* C + D. Execution status and stage results */}
681:       <Card>
682:         <CardHeader>
683:           <CardTitle>Consolidation stages</CardTitle>
684:           <CardDescription>
685:             Each stage reflects what the backend actually executed. Blocked
686:             stages require accounting services that are not yet implemented.
687:           </CardDescription>
688:         </CardHeader>
689:         <CardContent>
690:           {running ? (
691:             <div className="flex items-center gap-2 py-6 text-sm text-slate-500">
692:               <Loader2 className="size-4 animate-spin" aria-hidden />
693:               Executing the shared agent…
694:             </div>
695:           ) : readiness ? (
696:             <>
697:               <div className="divide-y divide-slate-100">
698:                 {readiness.stages.map((stage) => (
699:                   <StageRow key={stage.stage} stage={stage} />
700:                 ))}
701:               </div>
702:               {!readiness.complete ? (
703:                 <p className="mt-4 rounded-lg bg-slate-50 px-3 py-2 text-xs text-slate-600">
704:                   Consolidation is not complete: {readiness.blocked_stages.length}{" "}
705:                   required stage
706:                   {readiness.blocked_stages.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} remain
707:                   blocked and {readiness.pending_stages.length} pending.
708:                 </p>
709:               ) : null}
710:             </>
711:           ) : (
712:             <p className="py-2 text-sm text-slate-500">
713:               No run yet. Use{" "}
714:               <span className="font-medium text-slate-700">
715:                 Run Consolidation
716:               </span>{" "}
717:               to execute the FY2024 group consolidation.
718:             </p>
719:           )}
720:         </CardContent>
721:       </Card>
722: 
723:       <div className="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-2">
724:         {/* E. Issues */}
725:         <Card>
726:           <CardHeader>
727:             <CardTitle>Issues</CardTitle>
728:             <CardDescription>
729:               Accounting inconsistencies flagged by deterministic checks.
730:             </CardDescription>
731:           </CardHeader>
732:           <CardContent>
733:             {run && run.issues.length > 0 ? (
734:               <div>
735:                 {run.issues.map((issue, index) => (
736:                   <IssueRow key={`${issue.code}-${index}`} issue={issue} />
737:                 ))}
738:               </div>
739:             ) : run ? (
740:               <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">No issues reported.</p>
741:             ) : (
742:               <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">No run yet.</p>
743:             )}
744:           </CardContent>
745:         </Card>
746: 
747:         {/* F. Agent activity */}
748:         <Card>
749:           <CardHeader>
750:             <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
751:               <Bot className="size-4 text-slate-400" aria-hidden />
752:               Agent activity
753:             </CardTitle>
754:             <CardDescription>
755:               MCP tool calls recorded during the run, with status and duration.
756:             </CardDescription>
757:           </CardHeader>
758:           <CardContent>
759:             {run && run.tool_calls.length > 0 ? (
760:               <div>
761:                 {run.tool_calls.map((call, index) => (
762:                   <ToolCallRow key={`${call.name}-${index}`} call={call} />
763:                 ))}
764:               </div>
765:             ) : run ? (
766:               <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">No tool calls recorded.</p>
767:             ) : (
768:               <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">No run yet.</p>
769:             )}
770:           </CardContent>
771:         </Card>
772:       </div>
773: 
774:       {/* G. AI-assisted activity */}
775:       {run ? (
776:         <Card>
777:           <CardHeader>
778:             <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
779:               <Brain className="size-4 text-violet-500" aria-hidden />
780:               AI-assisted reasoning
781:             </CardTitle>
782:             <CardDescription>
783:               LLM-assisted stages run alongside the deterministic accounting.
784:               The LLM plans, investigates and proposes; Python performs every
785:               calculation and verifies every proposal. Nothing here replaces the
786:               deterministic result.
787:             </CardDescription>
788:           </CardHeader>
789:           <CardContent className="space-y-4">
790:             {!run.ai_configured ? (
791:               <div className="flex items-start gap-2 rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-slate-50 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-slate-600">
792:                 <ShieldAlert className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
793:                 <span>
794:                   AI is not available because no LLM credentials are configured.
795:                   Deterministic consolidation still ran; no AI activity is
796:                   reported.
797:                 </span>
798:               </div>
799:             ) : null}
800: 
801:             {run.ai_stages.length > 0 ? (
802:               <div className="divide-y divide-slate-100">
803:                 {run.ai_stages.map((stage) => (
804:                   <AIStageRow key={stage.stage} stage={stage} />
805:                 ))}
806:               </div>
807:             ) : (
808:               <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">
809:                 No AI stages recorded for this run.
810:               </p>
811:             )}
812: 
813:             {run.ai_reasoning.execution_plan?.summary ? (
814:               <div className="rounded-lg bg-slate-50 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-slate-700">
815:                 <span className="font-medium text-slate-800">Plan: </span>
816:                 {run.ai_reasoning.execution_plan.summary}
817:               </div>
818:             ) : null}
819: 
820:             {run.ai_reasoning.mapping_proposals &&
821:             run.ai_reasoning.mapping_proposals.length > 0 ? (
822:               <div>
823:                 <p className="mb-1 text-xs font-semibold tracking-wide text-slate-500 uppercase">
824:                   Proposed mapping decisions
825:                 </p>
826:                 {run.ai_reasoning.mapping_proposals.map((proposal, index) => (
827:                   <MappingProposalRow
828:                     key={`${proposal.entity}-${proposal.local_code}-${index}`}
829:                     proposal={proposal}
830:                   />
831:                 ))}
832:               </div>
833:             ) : null}
834: 
835:             {run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching?.proposals &&
836:             run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching.proposals.length > 0 ? (
837:               <div>
838:                 <p className="mb-1 text-xs font-semibold tracking-wide text-slate-500 uppercase">
839:                   Intercompany match proposals (deterministically verified)
840:                 </p>
841:                 {run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching.proposals.map(
842:                   (proposal, index) => (
843:                     <MatchProposalRow
844:                       key={`${proposal.left_row}-${proposal.right_row}-${index}`}
845:                       proposal={proposal}
846:                     />
847:                   ),
848:                 )}
849:                 {run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching.unmatched_notes &&
850:                 run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching.unmatched_notes.length >
851:                   0 ? (
852:                   <ul className="mt-2 list-disc space-y-1 pl-5 text-xs text-slate-500">
853:                     {run.ai_reasoning.intercompany_matching.unmatched_notes.map(
854:                       (note, index) => (
855:                         <li key={index}>{note}</li>
856:                       ),
857:                     )}
858:                   </ul>
859:                 ) : null}
860:               </div>
861:             ) : null}
862:           </CardContent>
863:         </Card>
864:       ) : null}
865: 
866:       {/* Trace events */}
867:       {trace && trace.events.length > 0 ? (
868:         <Card>
869:           <CardHeader>
870:             <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
871:               <RefreshCw className="size-4 text-slate-400" aria-hidden />
872:               Execution trace
873:             </CardTitle>
874:             <CardDescription>
875:               Persisted trace events for this run ({trace.trace_id}).
876:             </CardDescription>
877:           </CardHeader>
878:           <CardContent>
879:             <ol className="space-y-1.5">
880:               {trace.events.map((event) => (
881:                 <li
882:                   key={event.seq}
883:                   className="flex items-start gap-3 text-xs text-slate-600"
884:                 >
885:                   <span className="w-6 shrink-0 text-right font-mono text-slate-400">
886:                     {event.seq}

<｜DSML｜ parameter name="newString" string="true">@router.get("/output/{filename}")
async def download_output(filename: str) -> FileResponse:
    """Download one generated deliverable from the output directory.

    Only plain file names are accepted (no path separators), so a caller
    cannot traverse outside the configured output directory.
    """
    if (
        not filename
        or "/" in filename
        or "\\" in filename
        or ".." in filename
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="invalid file name")
    output_dir = Path(settings.output_dir).resolve()
    path = (output_dir / filename).resolve()
    if output_dir not in path.parents or not path.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="file not found")
    media_type = (
        "application/json" if filename.endswith(".json") else "text/csv"
    )
    return FileResponse(path, media_type=media_type, filename=filename)
